name: Paradoxornithidae
description: Parrotbills are a family of small to medium-sized passerine birds found primarily in East and Southeast Asia. They are named for their distinctive, parrot-like bills adapted for splitting bamboo stems and seed pods.

children.name: Chamaea
children.description: Chamaea — a genus in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Chamaea fasciata
children.description: The wrentit is a small bird that lives in chaparral, oak woodlands, and bushland on the western coast of North America. It is the only species in the genus Chamaea.

children.name: Paradoxornis
children.description: A genus of larger parrotbills with deep, robust bills, found in reed beds and bamboo across Asia.

children.name: Paradoxornis aemodium
children.description: The great parrotbill (Paradoxornis aemodius) is a bird species the Paradoxornithidae family. It is found in Bhutan, China, India, Myanmar, and Nepal. It was previously placed in a monotypic genus, the Conostoma.

children.name: Paradoxornis albirostris
children.description: A parrotbill with white bill from the Himalayas.

children.name: Paradoxornis alphonsianus
children.description: The ashy-throated parrotbill is a parrotbill. In old sources, it may be called Alphonse's crow-tit; though superficially resembling a tit it is not a member of the Paridae. The native range of this species extends from south-west China to northern Vietnam, and it might have become naturalised in one area in Italy.

children.name: Paradoxornis concolor
children.description: A rufous-headed parrotbill from the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Paradoxornis conspicillatus
children.description: The spectacled parrotbill (Suthora conspicillata) is a species of parrotbill bird in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Paradoxornis flaviventer
children.description: A parrotbill with yellow belly from the eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Paradoxornis gularis
children.description: The grey-headed parrotbill (Paradoxornis gularis) is a parrotbill in the family Sylviidae and is found in eastern Asia from the Himalayas to Indochina and Hainan.

children.name: Paradoxornis guttaticollis
children.description: The spot-breasted parrotbill (Paradoxornis guttaticollis) is a species of bird in the family Paradoxornithidae. It is found in Bangladesh, China, India, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand, and Vietnam.

children.name: Paradoxornis heudei
children.description: The reed parrotbill (Paradoxornis heudei) is a species of bird in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Paradoxornis marginatus
children.description: A parrotbill with spotted breast from southeastern Asia.

children.name: Paradoxornis nigriventris
children.description: A parrotbill with black throat from the Himalayas and western China.

children.name: Paradoxornis nipalensis
children.description: The black-throated parrotbill is a parrotbill species often placed with the Old World babblers or in a distinct family Sylviidae, but it actually seems to belong to the distinct family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Paradoxornis paradoxus
children.description: The three-toed parrotbill is a species of parrotbill in the family Paradoxornithidae. It is endemic to central China. Its natural habitat is temperate forests.

children.name: Paradoxornis poliotis
children.description: A parrotbill with grey head from southwestern China.

children.name: Paradoxornis ruficeps
children.description:
The white-breasted parrotbill (Paradoxornis ruficeps) is a bird species often placed with the Old World babblers (family Timaliidae) or in a distinct family Paradoxornithidae, but it actually seems to belong to the Sylviidae.
It is found in Eastern Himalaya, Myanmar, Laos and Vietnam. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Paradoxornis striatus
children.description: A striated parrotbill from central China.

children.name: Paradoxornis unicolor
children.description: The brown parrotbill (Paradoxornis unicolor) is a parrotbill found in the central and eastern Himalayas.

children.name: Paradoxornis webbianus
children.description: The vinous-throated parrotbill is a species of parrotbill in the family Paradoxornithidae; formerly, it was placed in the closely related Sylviidae or Timaliidae. It is found in China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Paradoxornis zapponi
children.description: A parrotbill from southern China and Vietnam.

children.name: Suthora
children.description: A genus of small parrotbills with short, deep bills, found in bamboo thickets across Asia.

children.name: Suthora webbiana
children.description: The vinous-throated parrotbill (Suthora webbiana) is a species of parrotbill in the family Paradoxornithidae; formerly, it was placed in the closely related Sylviidae or Timaliidae. It is found in China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Russia, Taiwan, and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Suthora alphonsiana
children.description: The ashy-throated parrotbill (Suthora alphonsiana) is a parrotbill. In old sources, it may be called Alphonse's crow-tit; though superficially resembling a tit it is not a member of the Paridae. The native range of this species extends from south-west China to northern Vietnam, and it might have become naturalised in one area in Italy.

children.name: Suthora nipalensis
children.description:
The black-throated parrotbill (Suthora nipalensis) is a parrotbill species often placed with the Old World babblers (family Timaliidae) or in a distinct family Sylviidae, but it actually seems to belong to the distinct family Paradoxornithidae.
It is found in the northern regions of the Indian subcontinent, primarily in the central and eastern Himalayas, and in adjoining parts of Southeast Asia. The species ranges across Bhutan, India, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal, Thailand, Tibet and Vietnam. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Suthora ruficeps
children.description: A parrotbill with rufous head from the Himalayas.

children.name: Suthora fulvifrons
children.description: The fulvous parrotbill (Suthora fulvifrons) is a species of parrotbill in the family Paradoxornithidae.

children.name: Suthora verreauxi
children.description: The golden parrotbill (Suthora verreauxi) is a species of parrotbill in the family Sylviidae.

children.name: Suthora princeps
children.description: A brown parrotbill from the Himalayas.

children.name: Suthora brunnea
children.description: The brown-winged parrotbill (Suthora brunnea) is a parrotbill that was formerly placed in the Old World babblers (family Timaliidae) or in the Sylviidae, but has been shown by molecular genetic studies to belong to the distinct family Paradoxornithidae. The eye-ringed parrotbill (Suthora ricketti) was formerly considered to be a subspecies.

children.name: Suthora zapponi
children.description: A parrotbill from southern China and Vietnam.

children.name: Suthora muriela
children.description: A parrotbill with black ear patch from western China.
